## Abstract

<!--
Provide a short (< 100 words), high-level description of the data. Additional details can be provided in README file(s) accompanying the materials.
-->
_To explore the usefulness of our proposed methodology, we analyze data of resting-state fMRI measurements over multiple subjects, sourced from_ (https://doi.org/10.6086/D1709N)[https://doi.org/10.6086/D1709N]. _After processing, the data includes measurements of brain activity for a total of 9 brain regions, over 150 time-points, for a total of 26 patients. We provide access to both the processed dataset, and reproducible R files to replicate our analysis. Data and code for analyzing can be found in our GitHub repository: _

[https://github.com/jsgomez94/ModVarCodeSubmission.git](https://github.com/jsgomez94/ModVarCodeSubmission.git)

# Part 2: Code

## Abstract

_There are two main components of our work which require the use of computational resources: (1) large scale simulation studies, and (2) analysis of multi-subject resting-state fMRI dataset with external moderators. For both  (1) and (2), we provide reproducible code and instructions to run the computational tasks on a linux-based computer cluster with the SLURM workload manager. _

_The code for reproducing all real-data analysis and numerical simulation studies can be found in our Supplementary Materials, in the form of a GitHub repository available here:_

[https://github.com/jsgomez94/ModVarCodeSubmission.git](https://github.com/jsgomez94/ModVarCodeSubmission.git)

_Descriptions on how to run the code can be found in the main _`README.md`_ file, as well as individual_ `README.md` _files that provide further details within each directory._

### Instructions

_The file _`./README.MD` _in our GitHub repository contains instructions for reproducing the figures included in our main paper and Supplementary Materials, except Figures 1 and 2. We provide the following clarification: Figures 3,4,5, 6 and 7 in the main text, as well as Figures S1-S15 in our Supplementary Materials are generated using a high-performing computational linux cluster with SLURM workload manager. In clusters with similar specifications, we provide instructions on how to reproduce the results. Figures 8 and 9 can be reproduced in a personal computer in between 1 and 10 minutes, if preprocessed results found in our GitHub repository are used. _
